rows.label: Sfx: Portcullis's cast, slam and close arms, before the shared rune-crack fallback
rows.why: The three Onslaught voices, in the synth only: new `w ===` arms placed BEFORE the shared rune-crack fallback, whose line is re-emitted unchanged, so another relic's row on the same anchor (Bindweed's voice rows use it) still applies, in either order. CAST, BAR of 5: a 600 Hz stone thunk (60 ms, dry), an iron bar struck on E4 (triangles on 1 : 2.76 : 5.40) and an A2-over-A1 hum settling -- audible 400 ms, TOP -2.7 dB re the hit @ 23, +18.9 re the wall, register at most 0.71 against rune-crack, the vigil and flail casts, the clank, death and the blow. SLAM, TOM of 4: a held E2 sine and E3 triangle cut together on a zero crossing at 0.194 s, a punch and a contact click; the gain a quadratic in p.shield (clamped 0..90) solved so the peak is 0.350 / 0.427 / 0.500 / 0.574 / 0.650 at 0 / 22.5 / 45 / 67.5 / 90 (the worst noise draw 0.011 off the line); LOW 0.84 at the worst draw (>= 0.45), gone 200 ms (<= 0.25 s), HOLD 0.95 and CUT 10 ms (gated). CLOSE, FALL of 3: three plate clinks, E6 / D6 / C6 at 0 / 0.10 / 0.23 s, 50 ms each. Through the patched play every arm reproduces its lab candidate to <= 1.2e-7 (the slam at ten shields), 125 other voices are unchanged (<= 1e-7), and ult/portcullis is no longer rune-crack (0.727).

rows.label: Sfx: the ward's bank voice -- a new kind, `ward-bank`, before hex-snap
rows.why: §7.2 says the bank is 'the ward's existing bank voice, reused'. There is none: the synth's 17 kinds have no ward or bank voice (a ward banks in silence; a ward that breaks plays the ordinary hit, a crit). So this is NEW -- `ward-bank`, the ward's own kind, as hex-snap is the runic school's -- inserted before hex-snap with that line re-emitted unchanged. LATCH of 4: C7 then E7 35 ms apart, struck ticks with a bar mode; audible 65 ms, +13.9 dB over the loudest slam in its own band (it lands on the slam's frame), -9.3 dB re the hit @ 23, +12.3 re the wall; register at most 0.48 (hex-snap), 0.21 against the spark collect (the blessing's chime). The SPARK and LONG controls fail its rule. Only Onslaught plays it (flagged: the vigil branch's own bank stays silent).

rows.label: tickRam: the slam voice, on the slam's frame, carrying the shield it hit for
rows.why: The slam's voice on the slam's own frame, right after `T.slams++;` (the anchor re-emitted first, unchanged), carrying `f.shield` -- the shield this slam hits for (0.25 x), before the bank adds 8 -- as a plain number in a fresh object literal (render.py keeps `p` by reference). It reads and writes nothing the sim uses. 148 fights: 2058 slams, 2058 slam voices, each on its slam's step; the bank voice that follows reads that shield + 8 (to the cap), which proves the slam carries the pre-bank shield. 38% of slams carry 0 (the quiet end, 0.35).

rows.label: tickRam: the ward's bank voice, after the bank's three writes
rows.why: The ward's bank voice after the bank's three writes, inside `if (u.bank > 0)` (the anchor re-emitted first, unchanged): once per bank, and every slam banks (the brief: 'Slams = banks'). At the cap the bank adds nothing but still restarts the ward's clock, and it still sounds -- a declared reading (23 of 2058 banks). 2058 banks, 2058 bank voices, on the slams' steps.

rows.label: tickRam: the close voice, when the window closes by its clock with the caster alive
rows.why: The close voice only when the window runs out by its clock with the caster alive (Zenith's, Daybreak's and Canopy's rule): one line placed BEFORE the window's own close line, which is re-emitted unchanged, so a picture row on that line still applies. 439 clock closes, 439 close voices; the 16 windows closed by the caster's death and the 73 ended by the fight play none. Rows 3-5 applied to tickRam's own source and run beside it: 148/148 fights identical (hp, shields, positions, velocities, clock, winner, the whole ramTally) and every other voice call identical in order, kind and opts; the same rows plus one sim write (the foe nudged 1e-9 on a slam) come back 3/148 identical, so the check can fail.

notes:
I resumed after the usage-limit break by starting this job again on the current tip. The only earlier work was a prototype in scratchpad/stage6/portcullis-voice/, run on sc-onslaught-b23, and none of it is used. The repo has only two new things: tools/portcullis_voice_lab.py (untracked) and 47 wavs in 05-reference/v100/ (gitignored). I did not touch git, 02-chain, CLAIMS.md or CLAUDE.md, and deleted my .pyc. At most one browser ran at a time.

The bank voice the design asks to reuse does not exist, so I made one and said so. §7.2 says a bank plays "the ward's existing bank voice, reused". The synth has 17 kinds and none is a ward or bank voice: a ward banks in silence, and a ward that breaks plays an ordinary crit hit. The new voice is its own kind, `ward-bank`, the way v88 gave the runic school `hex-snap`. Only Onslaught's bank plays it. The vigil branch's bank still makes no sound, because voicing it would change the sound of five shipped relics and no doc asks for that. Whether to do that is for Rick or Cowork.

The readings I chose are written in the lab's docstring:
- The slam carries f.shield from before the bank, which is what the slam hits for at 0.25 x shield. Mapping: peak 0.35 + 0.30 x shield/90, with the shield clamped to 0..90.
- The bank voice plays on every bank. Every slam banks ("Slams = banks"), including at the cap, where the bank adds nothing but restarts the ward's clock (23 of 2058 banks).
- The close plays only when the window closes by its clock with the caster alive, the Zenith/Daybreak/Canopy rule.
- The cast adds no sim line, since fireUlt already plays ult/portcullis.

Picks and the rules behind them follow Rick's "you pick i overrule". The rules and tiebreaks are written in the lab (*_RULE and *_why). Each voice has 3 to 5 candidates and controls that must come back wrong, and all of them did.

Six things were changed once after the first table, before any pick, and all six are listed in the lab:
- STONE instrument: the first version could not tell the no-stone control from the candidates.
- CLANG control: it passed METAL and RING on the hum's own triangle harmonics, so a LEADS gate was added.
- SETTLE: it was reading the silence after the voice.
- The stone constant: at first it could not be heard.
- The close tiebreak: it had fallen through to list order.
- Tolerance: raised from 1e-6 to 1e-5, because one render of the loudest slam through the compressor differed by 1.25e-6.

Rows and how they carry:
- All 5 rows are `replace`. Each anchor is unique in the tip, and each row puts its anchor back unchanged exactly once, so the rows apply on a tip that carries other relics.
- With the Portcullis picture rows in scratch (batch/portcullis/stage6-picture/rows_final.json): no shared anchors, and both orders give the same page. The combined picture+voice page loads with no errors, 74/74 fights match the tip, and slam and bank voices equal slams and banks.
- With the Bindweed picture rows: both orders give the same page.
- With Bindweed's voice rows2.json: they share only the rune-crack fallback anchor. Both orders apply, but the order of the arms depends on which set goes first. The arms are separate `w ===` branches, so the sound is the same either way.
